faqs.question: Who can pursue Film and Video Editing Courses?
faqs.answer: Aspirants who have a creative flair, as well as knowledge of design and video software, are apt to pursue a course in Film and Video Design. Candidates can pursue Film and Video Design courses at both UG and PG levels. To study Film and Video Design at the UG level, aspirants should have completed their 10+2 from a recognised board with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks . On the other hand, PG-level courses can be pursued by candidates if they possess a graduation degree in a similar field from a recognised college with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks.

faqs.question: What skills are required to pursue a Film and Video Design course?
faqs.answer: To make a career in the Film and Video Design field, you'll need to gain skills like: Eye for detail and precision. Strong vision to play out with scenes and colours. Strong communication skills to convey your creative ideas. Problem-solving abilities.

faqs.question: What is the scope of Film and Video Design courses?
faqs.answer: As a Film and Video Design students, you can opt for a job role as  an Art Director, Cinematographer, Film Director and Video Editor, etc . You can also become a freelance filmmaker or work in a production company. Some popular companies that offer jobs to Film and Video Design students include Channel V, Channel MTV, UTV Motion Pictures, Glitch Films and Supari Films.

faqs.question: Why should I opt for a Film and Video Design course?
faqs.answer: Here are some reasons why opting for a Film and Video Design programme is worth it. Creative Expression: Through the use of film and video design, people may visually tell stories, arouse feelings, and deliver messages. Multidisciplinary talents: Learning set design, costume design, graphic design, and cinematography are just a few of the multidisciplinary talents that come with pursuing film and video design. Story Telling: Facilitates the art of visual storytelling, in which designers are integral to the story's development through the production of visually captivating and engaging surroundings.

faqs.question: What is the minimum eligibility criteria for BDes in Film and Video Design?
faqs.answer: You can pursue BDes in Film and Video Design after completing Class 12,  3-year diploma, B.Voc or any other qualification that is equivalent to Class 12 with a minimum of 50% marks. You could have completed Class 12 in any stream and Diploma or B.Voc with any specialisation. It is required that you should have studied in a recognised educational institute.

faqs.question: Can I pursue MDes in Film and Video Design after completing BTech in Mechanical Engineering?
faqs.answer: Yes, you are eligible to pursue MDes in Film and Video Design after completing BTech in Mechanical Engineering . You can pursue the course after completing any undergraduate degree such BA, BSc, BTech/ BE etc. Since MDes is an advanced course, you are expected to have basic Design aptitude.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for BDes in Film and Video Design at LPU?
faqs.answer: The eligibility criteria for BDes in Film and TV Production at LPU are: Pass with 50% aggregate marks in 10+2 (with English) or equivalent. For a candidate, who has not studied English as a subject, the condition of English may be waived off provided the candidate in his qualifying exam has studied in English medium or an equivalent subject. (5% relaxation to North-East states and Sikkim candidates or Defence Personnel and their Dependents or Wards of Kashmiri Migrants).

faqs.question: What is the Film and Video Design Course admission process at MIT-ADT?
faqs.answer: Here's the  Film and Video Design Course admission process at MIT-ADT: Appear for MITID DET exam, based on scores obtained from MITID DET, shortlisted candidates will be called for second phase. Studio Test and Personal Interview is conducted at MITID campus in Pune. The second phase of the admission procedure will consist of studio tests followed by personal interviews at Institute in Pune. The result of shortlisted candidates for the Second Phase will be announced on MITID website. The Admission Committee decides the procedures, grades and weightage every year.

faqs.question: What is the admission process of BDes in Film and Video Design at LPU?
faqs.answer: Here are some steps you can follow to complete the admission process of BDes in Film and Video Design at LPU: Sign Up: Register onto LPUADMIT with basic details (Name, Email ID, Mobile No., State, Gender and Password). Your email id will act as your username for the portal and password will be set by you while registering on the portal. You will get a mail on your registered email id regarding this. Login to the LPUADMIT with already created username/ password. Take Admission: Fill the application form. Select your programme from the Available Programme List. Upload the documents. Apply for residential / mess / transportation / parking facility as per the requirement. All the submitted documents are to be verified from the originals within the prescribed timelines. Deposit the balance fee within the timelines prescribed by the university. Book the Exam Slot and Appear Book the slot to appear in the LPUNEST Exam. Appear and qualify for the exam. Perform STEP 2 in case admission is not taken already.

salary.title: Film and Video Design Career Scope: Job Profiles, Salary and Top Recruiters

blocks.value: People may explore a variety of interesting employment options in the vibrant and imaginative industry of filmmaking and visual storytelling after completing a study in film and video design. Pre-production, production, and post-production roles are all included in the career scope.
Know more about the Design Career Scope

Graduates or postgraduates in Film & Video Design can build their careers in the broad spectrum of the moving image industry including TV channels, feature films, advertising agencies, production houses, government agencies, corporate firms, etc. Some of the popular job profiles for Film and Video Design students are as follows.

value: A production designer creates and manages visual aspects of a film, television or theatre production. The professional works in coordination with the director and producer to create a design style for aspects such as graphics, sets, lighting, etc.

A cinematographer is a professional who manages camera and lighting crews and oversees the selection as well as the operation of technical equipment to create images. A cinematographer is responsible for the visual impact created by a film.

An art director is responsible for the overall visual aspects of a media or advertising campaign. Some of the daily responsibilities of an art director include coordinating the work of other design staff such as graphic designers and hiring as well as supervising assistant art directors.
A video editor edits and assembles recorded raw material (such as camera footage, dialogue, special effects etc) into a suitable and finished product ready for broadcasting.
A filmmaker usually refers to the director or producer of a film. A filmmaker is a person who is responsible for taking a film from the development stage to the finished product.

faqs.question: What is the salary of a Video Editor?
faqs.answer: The salary offered to a Video Editor varies depending on the project they are working for as well as the company for which they work. As per Naukri.com, on average film and video designers earn between INR 25,000 to INR 75,000 per month. A Title Designer is someone who is responsible for creating the opening title sequence and title cards for a television show or film. A title designer is also responsible for creating end credits for the film/video piece.

faqs.question: What is the salary offered to VFX Artists and Scriptwriters?
faqs.answer: Entry-level VFX artists may earn wages ranging from INR 2 - 5 Lacs per year. Experienced VFX supervisors or leaders may receive a higher salary. Scriptwriters may be compensated based on the intricacy of the script and the production budget. Entry-level scriptwriters may make a modest salary, although experienced and accomplished scriptwriters might fetch larger rates.

faqs.question: Which is the highest-paying job in the Film and Video Design industry?
faqs.answer: In the Film and Video Design industry, the highest-paying roles generally include Film Producers, Directors, Screenwriters, Senior Editors, etc. The average package of a Director is INR 53.4 Lakhs depending on the project size. To gain relevant experience in the industry with better packages, you can also go for freelance projects.

faqs.question: What are the latest trends in the Film and Video Design industry?

blocks.value: Here are some popular Film and Video trends:

value: Ephemeral Videos : Instagram, Snapchat, and WhatsApp stories that disappear after 24 hours are ephemeral videos. The trend of these video stories was a hit in 2024 and continue in 2025.

Reels : Short vertical videos on social media platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube have created hype around the globe. Millions of internet users including celebrities, sportspersons, etc., create and upload these kinds of videos in different niches.
